title: What became of Peter Bocage's music
summary: Peter's son keeps all the music and instruments and will not share; Peter wrote out numbers for the band; copying can be done cheaply.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Do you know what happened to all the music he had?
He left about thirty thousand dollars in it. Yeah.
Do you know what happened to the music that he had? All the sheet music? Music? Peter's music? Yeah.
Well, I guess his boy got all that.
Yeah.
But you see... His boy still lives there.
Yeah, his son lives there.

But you see, his son ain't gonna give away nothing like that. He ain't gonna get rid of that music, because he... Percy had wanted to get Peter's mouthpiece off his trumpet, you know? Yeah. Because Percy talked to me about it one day. He told me, he said, As fun as you think I could get Peter's mouthpiece. He said, I liked it, that mouthpiece that Peter had. So... I told him, I said, Percy, you're gonna have a hard time, I said, because that boy ain't gonna let none of these poor things out. Yeah.
He just... Well, he's not used?

No, he got... He got all these poor stuff right up there now. He's got the drum boy, he got his... He wants to keep everything. He's low boy using his dad his trumpet, or his son. Yeah. Peter's grandson, he played trumpet. He's in the... But he's in the ringing band.
Why does he want to keep all the music? Why does he want to keep the music?

He's not gonna use the music. No, that's just it. I don't know why he won't keep it. I told him, because a couple of fellas came over here one time and went there to try to see could they get some of that music from him, but he wouldn't let none of them...
It's just gonna get ruined there. Yeah. See his band, tell him some of the numbers your band plays. Yeah.

Yeah, we play some of that kind of music, you know. My band, my band, we play some of the old music. Play some of that old music. Yeah, but I would be interested, you know, to find... Yeah, yeah. See some of Pete's music.

He plays all those Scott Joplin numbers and everything. Yeah. You remember Scott Joplin's numbers? Who? Scott Joplin! Yeah. Maple Leaf Rag he plays. You remember Maple Leaf? Yeah. He plays all those old numbers in his band. Yeah.
Say it all, man.
He's got Fairboss on trumpet, you know Lionel Fairboss?
Well, all them old numbers, I tell you, sounds good sometimes when you knock them off, you know. I'd rather hear them some of them old numbers than hear them new numbers they got up now.
Oh, yeah. Well, the music makes sense.
Yeah. Yeah. Well, we wanted to see if we could get some of Pete's music, you know, or make copies of it. Yeah. But it looked like, you know, you don't want to let it out.

Well, you see how we used to do. When we had our little band up like that, we had a little reader there, Peter's little boy used to play trumpet too, you know. Well, I used to play with him sometimes. Well, we'd go out and play a dance like that, somebody come ask for a number and we don't have it. We'd come back, Peter would write that number out for us. You see? He'd write that number out and we'd go back again, boy, play it.
You know, there's a place right down the street, that guy Earl Schmidt, he's a lawyer.
Who?
There's a lawyer named Earl Schmidt right down the street and he'll make copies for ten cents a page. Yeah.
You see that, Lars? Yeah.
For ten cents a page, he'll make copies of it. In Algiers, you could get it done.
What instrument do you play? Piano. Piano. And guitar?
